subject: MSA & Order Form — renewal trigger and offboarding matrix alignment
messages:
From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@datasourceinc.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@datasourceinc.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on MSA/Order Form — renewal triggers & termination mechanics

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked I follow up with a few specific questions on the MSA + Order Form language before we loop legal into a formal redline:

1) Auto-renew: We currently see an auto-renew clause for 12 months unless 30 days' notice is given. Our internal policy prefers a 90-day opt-out window for enterprise agreements. Is Redwood open to moving to 90 days?

2) Termination for convenience: We need clarity on transition support and fees if either party terminates for convenience mid-term. Ben wants to understand what operational support is included and how billing is prorated.

3) Notice windows: Procurement typically wants a standard 60-day notice for material changes, and a 90-day notice for renewals. Can you confirm which windows apply to which events?

If it's easier, we can have your legal send a redline and we'll respond, but wanted to surface preferences early.

Best,
Alice
Procurement Manager
DataSource Inc.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@datasourceinc.com>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@datasourceinc.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA/Order Form — renewal triggers & termination mechanics

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: we can be flexible but need to balance SRE commitments and committed capacity pricing. I'll loop in Legal (Kimberly) and Pricing (Karthik) to draft a pragmatic compromise and capture transition obligations.

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly: can you prepare a redline that shows both 30- and 90-day renewal notice options and a suggested compromise?
- Karthik/Marissa: we'll run the cost sensitivity (how 90-day opt-out affects reserved pricing) and call out any minimums.
- Alice/Ben: if you can confirm whether DataSource expects full handover support (e.g., on-prem export, KV cache purge, playbook) vs. only standard export and final invoices, that will help.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with procurement + our legal next week once we have an initial redline.

Thanks —
Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on MSA/Order Form — renewal triggers & termination mechanics

Team / Alice —

Attached is a first-pass redline of the MSA and sample Order Form language (MSA_redlines_kp_20251002.docx). Key points we included and questions for procurement:

- Renewal notice: we drafted two alternatives in the MSA: (A) 30-day opt-out for standard hosted tiers; (B) 90-day opt-out for reserved/dedicated capacity or enterprise agreements. The idea is to let customers opt into a 90-day commitment in exchange for pricing protections.

- Auto-renew term: we kept the 12-month renewal period but added an explicit clause that any short-term pilots (<= 3 months) default to a 3-month renewal unless otherwise specified in the Order Form.

- Termination for convenience: proposed mutual right with the following guardrails:
  * 60 days' written notice for convenience termination by either party;
  * Customer is entitled to (i) export of data and KV cache within 30 days, (ii) optionally purchase a 90-day transition support package (priced in Order Form), and (iii) proration of pre-paid fees on a per-day basis for unused portion of the billing period.

Open questions for Procurement:
1) If DataSource requires a guaranteed 90-day notice for renewals, do they want that to be universal or only for certain product lines?
2) What level of transition support (no-cost vs. paid add-on) is a hard requirement?

I'll wait for procurement to confirm requirements then we'll produce a clean/marked copy for signature.

Attachments: MSA_redlines_kp_20251002.docx (redline)

- Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Torres <ben.torres@datasourceinc.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Huang <alice.huang@datasourceinc.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on MSA/Order Form — renewal triggers & termination mechanics

Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks for the redline. A few clarifications from DataSource procurement/legal:

- Renewal notice: we would prefer the 90-day renewal opt-out to apply to the overall customer agreement (not segmented by product), given we often bundle services across platforms. If Redwood insists on segmenting, we will need clear language in the Order Form that the customer can elect the 90-day enterprise cadence as a single toggle.

- Termination for convenience: the 60-day notice is acceptable, but the final handover must include at least 60 days of operational transition support at no additional charge (we request the first 60 days free, after which paid support options are available). This is non-negotiable for us due to data handling and decommission timelines.

- Billing proration: we agree to per-day proration for pre-paid fees. We also request a defined offboarding checklist (export formats, logs, KV cache snapshot) be referenced in the MSA or an annex.

We'll review Kimberly's redline and provide inline comments in the doc.

Ben
Director, IT Procurement
DataSource Inc.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@datasourceinc.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@datasourceinc.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — renewal trigger and offboarding matrix alignment

Alice/Ben —

Thanks for the clear feedback. Quick summary and proposed path forward that tries to meet you halfway:

1) Renewal notice: commit to a single Order Form toggle that elects enterprise cadence (90-day renewal opt-out) for the entire Agreement when selected at signature. Default remains 30 days for standard hosted subscriptions.

2) Termination for convenience: agree to mutual 60-day written notice. To address DataSource's operational needs, Redwood will include a 60-day complimentary transition assistance package (standard tasks: export of account data, KV cache snapshot, runbook handoff, and decommission checklist). Additional transition services beyond that will be offered as paid support.

3) Billing proration: agree to per-day proration for pre-paid fees; we'll add specific calculation examples to the MSA annex so procurement has certainty.

I've attached a short offboarding-runbook template (offboarding-runbook_20251007.xlsx) we plan to reference in the annex. Next steps: Kimberly will produce a clean redline reflecting the Order Form toggle and the explicit 60-day complimentary transition package; once we agree we can route to DocuSign. Proposed legal sync: Thu, Oct 9 at 10am PT — Marcus will send a calendar invite if that works.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this with your team.

Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachment: offboarding-runbook_20251007.xlsx (template)
